definition: topic_consistency — continuity with the input: the share of the output's content-bearing sentences that connect to the input's topic must be at least a third (config key topic_consistency, default 0.33). A sentence connects when it shares a content term with the input or with an earlier connected sentence; list items are read under the sentence that introduces them; outputs with fewer than six words of four or more letters are skipped rather than judged. Definition version: docs/api-reference.md §Relevance Rules and the rule description as merged in #416 (9d9fd50) on 2026-09-04, which replaced the share-of-output-words-found-in-the-input measure. Positive = fewer than a third of the content sentences connect (the rule should FAIL).
source: LLM-authored on 2026-09-04. Held out on 2026-09-23: the 10 case(s) copied from, varied from or modelled on the 24 real transcripts in tests/fixtures/real-transcripts (topic-001, topic-002, topic-003, topic-004, topic-005, topic-006, topic-007, topic-008, topic-009, topic-010) were removed, so no number this family publishes is estimated on a transcript, and the transcript line in proof/TRANSCRIPTS.md and proof/COMPOSITE.md is measured on cases none of these rates were estimated from. 3 replacement case(s), authored the same day and marked in their notes, bring the family back to the 24-case floor the runner enforces. The replacements sit far from the threshold (0% or 100% under any reasonable reading), so their labels do not depend on this file's particular stopword or sentence lists.
labelling: LLM-authored on 2026-09-04 and labelled against the documented definition. First labelled that morning semantically against the definition then documented (5% of output words found in the input, purpose "stays on topic"); re-labelled the same day, after #416 replaced the mechanism with sentence continuity, by applying the new documented definition independently by script — its sentence splitting, content-term lists and inflection folding are this file's own reading, not the rule's — with each note stating the connected/total count that decided the label. Consequences a reader should know: an off-target real answer that reuses the question's vocabulary connects (the real transcripts t-17 and t-18 do), and an on-topic answer in fresh words does not (three such cases are positive; the documentation states this lexical limit). 0 case(s) landed between 20% and 45% under this reading and were dropped as undecidable from the documentation alone: none. Four cases whose point was that a shared word is not topical relevance (history of the same product, business retention for a database question) were removed because the documented definition explicitly reads a shared term as connection, so they cannot be labelled positive under it.
